name: James Tuttle
bioAdditions: A 'James Tuttle' signed the 1775 Articles of Association in Cornwall Precinct with Thomas Lamoureux and John Tuthill (S1). Note the namesake cousin 'James Tuttle, junr.' at Brookhaven c.1738/9, who is the uncle James Jr. (d. 1756), not this man (S2).

sources.citation: Ruttenber & Clark, History of Orange County (1881), Articles of Association 1775, Cornwall Precinct signers (c. pp. 68-69)

Records of the Town of Brookhaven, Suffolk County, N.Y. (printed 1880; volume covering the 1720s-1750s), p. 113 (1 May 1721 land laid out to James Tuthill on the other half of Dayton's Right, 22 1/2 acres east of his Chestnut Pound land, plus 9 1/2 acres on John Roe's right, adjoining his former 50 lot), pp. 139-140 (10 June 1737 highway across the north ends of the 15-acre lots in Fireplace Neck, laid out at the request of owners incl. 'Jeames Tuttel', beginning at the westernmost 15-acre lot 'now belonging to Jeames Tuttel'), p. 143 ('James Tuttle, junr.' among signers, c. 1738/9), pp. 147-148 (award of arbitrators Isaac Browne, William Smith, James Tuthill and Richard Woodhull, sealed 5 Oct 1741), p. 166 (c. 1750 road between Thomas Rose's and James Tuthill's land in Fireplace Neck)
